newsitem.title: USA: U.S. debt futures decline late to finish lower.
newsitem.headline: U.S. debt futures decline late to finish lower.

text.p: U.S. debt futures slipped late to end in lower territory after spending much of the day caught near steady.

Traders said three Wall Street firms sold 1,000 contracts each in December Treasury bonds in the last 15 minutes of trading, jarring debt futures from their day-long slumber. Because of the empty economic line-up and impending mid-week Treasury auctions, trading pits were thin, traders said. The thin pits and nervousness after the market failed late Friday on the week's high magnified the weakness, traders said.
Selling from a prominent local added pressure, they said.
Treasury will auction $18.25 billion in two-year notes on Tuesday and $12.5 billion in five-year notes on Wednesday.
Still, support at 111-00 held and one trader called the late decline "nothing too dramatic."
Traders noted that December Treasury bonds still closed well above the 200-day moving average at 110-16/32.
"The closes are still above the 200-day moving average and that's what a lot of technicians are looking at," the bond trader said.
He pegged support at 110-20/32, with others putting support at 110-30/32.
"111-00 keeps us in pretty good shape," another trader said.
Jim Hyerczyk, president of JAH Research and Trading, said a close below 110-27/32 on Tuesday would be a bearish sign for December T-bonds.

"It looks like there's a double top formation and it's under 90-day cycle pressure," he said. "If it breaks under 110-27/32 tomorrow that would be a negative sign and there's plenty of room on the downside," he said.
Hyerczyk said 109-26/32 must hold to keep the trend bullish.

December T-bonds settled down 7/32 at 111-2/32, T-notes lost 5/32 to 108-16/32, muni-bonds lost 19/32 to 114-6/32, March T-bills dropped two basis points to 94.83 and March Eurodollars fell one basis point to 94.31. -Derivatives Desk(312)408-8750/E-mail:derivatives@reuters.com
